issue_context.title: Convert to GeneratedRegexAttribute fixer should preserve references to const string fields
issue_context.body:
Regex patterns typically contain plenty of backslashes. The fixer doubles them up. Consider
```c#
    private const string patt = @"\s*";
    private static Regex r1 = new Regex(patt);
```
run the fixer, you get
```c#
    [GeneratedRegex("\\s*")]
    private static partial Regex MyRegex();
```
it would have been clearer to use an @ string like this:
```c#
    [GeneratedRegex(@"\s*")]
    private static partial Regex MyRegex();
```
that might not seem a big deal, but now consider this output from running it on a particular regex in dotnet/msbuild
```c#
            [GeneratedRegex("((?<=@\\(\\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*\\s*->\\s*'[^']*)%\\(\\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*)\\s*\\.\\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*) \\s*\\)(?![^']*'(\\s*,\\s*'[^']*')?\\s*\\))) | ((?<!@\\(\\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*\\s*->\\s*'[^']*)%\\(\\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*)\\s*\\.\\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*) \\s*\\)(?=[^']*'(\\s*,\\s*'[^']*')?\\s*\\))) | ((?<!@\\(\\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*\\s*->\\s*'[^']*)%\\(\\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*)\\s*\\.\\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\\-]*) \\s*\\)(?![^']*'(\\s*,\\s*'[^']*')?\\s*\\)))", RegexOptions.ExplicitCapture | RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace)]
            private static partial Regex MyRegex1();
```
which is considerably less easy to read than the below, which can also be pasted into a regex explainer site, eg.
```c#
            [GeneratedRegex(@"((?<=@\(\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*\s*->\s*'[^']*)%\(\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*)\s*\.\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*) \s*\)(?![^']*'(\s*,\s*'[^']*')?\s*\))) | ((?<!@\(\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*\s*->\s*'[^']*)%\(\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*)\s*\.\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*) \s*\)(?=[^']*'(\s*,\s*'[^']*')?\s*\))) | ((?<!@\(\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*\s*->\s*'[^']*)%\(\s* (?<ITEM_SPECIFICATION>(?<ITEM_TYPE>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*)\s*\.\s*)? (?<NAME>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9\-]*) \s*\)(?![^']*'(\s*,\s*'[^']*')?\s*\)))", RegexOptions.ExplicitCapture | RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace)]
            private static partial Regex MyRegex1();
```
If Roslyn doesn't have a built-in way to translate, I imagine the fixer would replace all `\\` with `\` and put an `@` on the front.

This should have been fixed by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/78172. Was it not?

No, that only fixed the literal case --- `new Regex(@"\s*");`

The tests added in that change demonstrate that it does _not_ work for fields/locals -- note that the @ is lost here:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7853356ab6989eba20f8cb67abe174e2c0a401ac/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/tests/FunctionalTests/UpgradeToGeneratedRegexAnalyzerTests.cs#L892

the code goes here
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7853356ab6989eba20f8cb67abe174e2c0a401ac/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/gen/UpgradeToGeneratedRegexCodeFixer.cs#L277-L284

and argument.Value is a LocalReferenceOperation or FieldReferenceOperation, which are not ILiteralOperation's, so the condition is not satisfied.

> No, that only fixed the literal case

Right. You're instead talking about a case where it's referring to a const string defined separately? I think such a case should generate code that refers to the exact same const if its in scope or else the fix shouldn't be offered. We shouldn't be duplicating the literal, regardless of slashes, nor should we be deleting a const something else may be referencing or even if it's not that was explicitly outlined by the developer.

> I think such a case should generate code that refers to the exact same const if its in scope or else the fix shouldn't be offered.

That sounds good to me.

review_comments: What about if it's a const declared on another class, e.g. `new Regex(SomethingElse.Pattern)`?
Do we have a test that validates it does the "right thing" if the const is local to the method instead?

If by the right thing, you mean that the local const literal should not be referenced inside GeneratedRegex (because it's out of scope). I think this test does the job :

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/58d1ecb3e50ead5cd48752bbaedf6dc23ccd2523/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/tests/FunctionalTests/UpgradeToGeneratedRegexAnalyzerTests.cs#L948-L979

> I think this test does the job

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1eed062e48750b60eea5f201ca8c975548b2ad27/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/tests/FunctionalTests/UpgradeToGeneratedRegexAnalyzerTests.cs#L975-L976

Isn't that test supposed to generate code that refers to the exact same const? i.e:
```cs
    [GeneratedRegex(pattern2)]
    private static partial Regex MyRegex();
```
@pedrobsaila could you cover this scenario?

> Isn't that test supposed to generate code that refers to the exact same const? i.e:

no because pattern2 is local variable to Main, it can't be referenced outside the method if I'm not mistaken
Ah right, then could you fix the double slushes issue and keep `@""a|b\s\n""`?
my bad forgot about that :) , I'll do it
